text: You wake up feeling unwell, and all you want is to see a doctor, right now. You need help, and quickly.
But when you call, they don't say "come right in." Instead, you're offered a specific time slot, perhaps days away.
It feels frustrating. Why can't you just show up and be seen first-come, first-served? You might think it's just bad organization.
This isn't just a queue; it's a system. Appointment slots balance unpredictable patient demand with limited doctor availability, ensuring dedicated time for your care.
The "cost" is waiting longer *before* your visit, but the gain is a much shorter, more focused wait *during* your visit. This system avoids chaotic clinic waits.
So next time you book, you'll still feel the initial wait. But now you understand it's a clever design, making sure everyone gets efficient, quality care.
